155869-personal-hotspot-isn-t-working.why: Airplane Mode only if issues remain
155869-personal-hotspot-isn-t-working.text:
It's possible that devices can connect to your Personal Hotspot, but you have a weak or problematic cellular connection that's affecting your devices' performance.
Try turning off your Personal Hotspot temporarily and use your iPhone as you normally would. Make sure you're not connected to a Wi-Fi network and try placing a call or loading a webpage.
If you're encountering issues, try switching your phone to Airplane Mode, waiting 15 seconds, and turning it off. Otherwise, try moving to a location with a stronger or more consistent cellular signal and testing Personal Hotspot again to see if the issue is with your iPhone's connection or the hotspot.

155842-wi-fi-calling-isn-t-working.why: Airplane Mode is an optional test
155842-wi-fi-calling-isn-t-working.text:
Take a moment to check that Wi-Fi calling is enabled on your device. You'll also want to confirm that your carrier and service plan includes Wi-Fi Calling.
When you enable Wi-Fi Calling, you'll likely be prompted to enter your permanent address. If you can't do this within your iPhone's interface, check to see if you need to do this within your carrier's account settings (on its website or mobile app).
To test if Wi-Fi calling works, simply enable Airplane Mode on your iPhone and attempt to make a phone call while connected to a Wi-Fi network.

156125-battery-draining-too-quickly.text:
If you're still encountering issues with your battery, and that hasn't been resolved by any of the previous steps, restarting your iPhone, or using different cables to charge your device, you may need to set up a service appointment at an Apple Genius Bar or other Authorized Service Provider.
Similarly, if your iPhone is reporting an issue with your Battery Health, or your iPhone is recommending service for your battery, you'll want to consider replacing your battery to restore your device's performance and total capacity.
